name: Boghom
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Michael Bulkaam. 2021. An introduction to Mantsi, a South Bauchi language of Central Nigeria. Draft circulated for comment, Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, 1 Jan 2021 (Internet Archive copy of rogerblench.info B3/Mantsi).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology section (2.1-2.3) is for Mantsi [zns], a sister language in the Kir subgroup: 'Mantsi has three level tones as well as rising and falling'; no mention of stress/accent. Boghom appears only in the references (Cosper n.d. ms wordlist incl. Boghom; Cosper 1999).

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2009. Documenting linguistic varieties of the South-Bauchi group. HAL halshs-00647808.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Boghom data; Boghom only in bibliography (Cosper title). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2005. Les Zaars et leurs voisins. HAL halshs-00643986.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists 'boghom' as Shimizu's South Bauchi cluster 1; the paper treats only South-Bauchi-West languages. Nothing on Boghom stress.

sources.citation: Caron, Bernard. 2002. Review of 'Barawa lexicon: a wordlist of eight South Bauchi (West Chadic) languages: Boghom, Buli, Dott, Geji, Sayanci and Zul' by Ronald Cosper, Munich: LINCOM EUROPA, 1999. Chadic Newsletter 23: 46-80 (HAL halshs-00644636).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Reports that Cosper 1999 'gives the chart of phonemes for the eight languages' (incl. Boghom) and marks two tones; criticises tone marking. No Boghom prosody statement.

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1975. Boghom and Zaar: Vocabulary and Notes. Kano: Centre for the Study of Nigerian Languages. 40 pp.

sources.note: Glottolog's sole grammar sketch for bogh1241; 'Notes' likely cover phonology incl. tone and possibly stress.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann. 1964/65. Materialien zur Kenntnis des Chip, Montol, Gerka und Burrum (Südplateau, Nordnigerien). Afrika und Übersee 48: 161-182.

sources.note: Only descriptive treatment of Boghom (as 'Burrum') by a Chadicist with grammatical notes; Jungraithmayr's Materialien sketches usually include Ton/Akzent remarks — most likely place for an explicit stress/accent sentence.
